commands.summary: List every user with its state (administrators; one page, --all follows next_cursor).

commands.name: user disable
commands.summary: Disable a user (administrators; never past the last administrator or a last Owner, FG-AUTH-0009). Its tokens and sessions end. Needs --yes.

commands.name: user sessions
commands.summary: List a user's active web sessions (administrators).

commands.name: user end-sessions
commands.summary: End every web session of a user (administrators). Needs --yes.

commands.name: token list
commands.summary: List your personal access tokens (never a secret; revoked and expired ones too).

commands.name: token revoke
commands.summary: Revoke one of your tokens (it may be the one gstn uses). Needs --yes.

commands.name: notifications get
commands.summary: Show your notification settings: mail on or off, the language of the mail (null: the instance default), the kinds muted, in-app on or off and its muted kinds; kinds lists every kind there is.

args.description: A kind to stop (repeatable; notifications get lists them).
args.name: --mute

commands.name: notifications set
commands.summary: Change your notification settings; a flag changes only what it names (the rest is kept). Nobody else's can be changed, administrators included.

args.description: Only older than this id (next_before of the previous page).
args.name: --before

commands.name: notifications list
commands.summary: List your in-app notifications, newest first: only those whose merge request you may still read (a page may hold fewer than --limit); next_before pages back.

commands.name: notifications count
commands.summary: How many of your in-app notifications are unread (those you may still see; at most 100 counted, capped says when more exist).

commands.name: notifications read
commands.summary: Mark one of your in-app notifications read, or every unread one with --all (somebody else's is not found).

commands.name: admin service-account list
commands.summary: List every service account with its owner, state and token summary (administrators; at most 500, truncated says when more exist).

commands.name: admin service-account view
commands.summary: Show one service account: owner, purpose, active tokens and the latest expiry (administrators; a person's id is not found).

args.description: Why it exists (1..=500 characters, one line).
args.name: --purpose

args.description: The new owner's user id (an active person).
args.name: --owner

commands.name: admin service-account update
commands.summary: Change a service account's display name, purpose or owner (administrators, people only; offboarding hands it on with --owner).

commands.name: admin service-account tokens
commands.summary: List a service account's tokens with who issued them (administrators; never a secret; revoked and expired ones too).

commands.name: admin service-account revoke-token
commands.summary: Revoke one of a service account's tokens at once, e.g. after a leak (administrators; an admin-scoped token works). Needs --yes.

commands.name: admin integration list
commands.summary: List every integration with its kind, service account, state and binding count (administrators, people only; at most 500, truncated says when more exist).

commands.name: admin integration view
commands.summary: Show one integration: kind, service account, enabled, event type allowlist, binding count (administrators, people only).

commands.name: admin integration bindings
commands.summary: List the projects bound to an integration with their external project ids (administrators, people only; at most 200).

args.description: The cursor the feed gave (next_cursor, an event's cursor, or integration cursor); without it the oldest retained event.
args.name: --cursor

commands.name: integration events
commands.summary: One page of an integration's event feed after a cursor: every integration-class event of its bound projects in order, each with its work items (the integration's own service account token, read_api; FG-INT-0007 410 with reason when the cursor cannot continue, FG-INT-0008 for a cursor that is not this integration's).

commands.name: integration cursor
commands.summary: The head of an integration's event feed as a cursor (a resync takes it first, then the development status, then reads from it; the integration's own service account token).

args.description: The kanflow project id of the binding (default: every bound one).
args.name: --project-id

commands.name: integration dev-status
commands.summary: One work item's development status (M3 I1d): the merge requests linked to PBI-<n> across the integration's bound projects — open, merged and closed — with approvals, the head's checks (checks_state none is no run, never success) and as_of_seq / feed_cursor (the integration's own service account token, read_api; FG-REPO-0005 for a reference of no bound kanflow project).

commands.name: integration dev-status-list
commands.summary: One page of every work item's development status (M3 I1d; the resync after a 410: integration cursor first, then these pages until next_cursor is null, then integration events from that cursor or feed_cursor; FG-INT-0007 410 when the walk cannot continue).

commands.name: integration-binding list
commands.summary: Show a project's integration binding, none or one (as reading the project).

args.description: The external project's id (A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -, at most 100).
args.name: --external-project

commands.name: integration-binding set
commands.summary: Bind a project to an external (kanflow) project of an integration (people only; Maintainer). Its service account becomes a Reporter of the project; a project already bound elsewhere is FG-INT-0016, a 201st binding of the integration FG-INT-0012. Binding again to the same external project answers unchanged.

commands.name: integration-binding remove
commands.summary: Unbind a project from an integration (people only; Maintainer); the Reporter membership the binding granted is removed. Needs --yes.

commands.name: admin service-account check-grants
commands.summary: The check namespaces a service account may report, per project (M3 C1; administrators).

args.description: The project the grant is for.
args.name: --project

commands.name: admin service-account grant-checks
commands.summary: Let a service account report checks of a namespace (ci or kanflow) on one project (administrators, people only). A grant is for that project only, and the account must also be a Developer member there; forge/ and ext/ are never granted.

args.description: The project the grant is for.
args.name: --project

commands.name: admin service-account revoke-checks
commands.summary: Stop a service account reporting checks of a namespace on one project (administrators, people only); its reported runs stay.

args.description: The full commit id (40 or 64 hex digits).
args.name: --sha

args.description: <namespace>/<name>, e.g. ci/gates (keep it stable per kind of check).
args.name: --name

args.description: With completed: success, neutral, failure, error or action_required.
args.name: --conclusion

args.description: The summary from a UTF-8 file (at most 64 KiB).
args.name: --summary-file

args.description: An http(s) link for people (the server never fetches it).
args.name: --details-url

args.description: A JSON array of {path, start_line, end_line?, level, message, title?} (at most 50).
args.name: --annotations-file

examples: gstn checks report --project 7 --sha 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 --name ci/gates --status completed --conclusion success --details-url https://ci.example.test/runs/1
commands.name: checks report
commands.summary: Report a check run on a commit (M3 C1, docs/api/checks.md): a service account holding the name's namespace (ci/, kanflow/) and a Developer member; the same name on the same commit updates its run (there is no separate update). A conclusion exactly with --status completed. The commit must be reachable from a branch or tag (otherwise not found, FG-REPO-0023). A required check of a protected branch is met only by completed/success on the merge request's head.

args.description: The full commit id (40 or 64 hex digits).
args.name: --sha

commands.name: checks list
commands.summary: Every check run of a commit, by name, with its annotations (as the repository browse API; schema_version 1).

commands.name: webhook list
commands.summary: A project's webhooks (Maintainer): URL, event types, enabled, the failure count; never a secret.

commands.name: webhook event-types
commands.summary: The event types a webhook may name, each with its class (integration, maintainer, deployment), and per class whether you may subscribe (Maintainer).

commands.name: webhook view
commands.summary: One webhook of a project (Maintainer); disabled_reason says why it is off (manual, failures, failing_24h).

args.description: An event type, a family (merge_request.*) or * (repeatable; default *).
args.name: --event

commands.name: webhook create
commands.summary: Create a webhook owned by you (a person; Maintainer). The URL must be https and on the operator's allowlist (400 FG-INT-0010 otherwise; loopback, link-local and metadata addresses never). The secret is shown once: give it to the receiver, which verifies Forge-Signature.

args.description: A new https URL (the allowlist again).
args.name: --url

commands.name: webhook update
commands.summary: Change a webhook's URL or event types (replaced), or enable / disable it; --enable clears the failure count (a person; Maintainer).

commands.name: webhook delete
commands.summary: Delete a webhook and its delivery history (a person; Maintainer). Needs --yes.

commands.name: webhook rotate-secret
commands.summary: Replace a webhook's secret, shown once; the previous secret still signs for 24 hours (two v1 values in Forge-Signature) so the receiver can switch (a person; Maintainer).

args.description: Only deliveries older than this delivery id.
args.name: --before

commands.name: webhook deliveries
commands.summary: A webhook's delivery history, newest first: state, attempts, the last status, reason and FG code (never a body; Maintainer).

commands.name: webhook redeliver
commands.summary: Deliver one delivery again with the same Forge-Delivery id (a person; Maintainer). 429 while it is pending or within 60 s of its last attempt.

commands.name: mirror show
commands.summary: A project's push mirror to GitLab (administrators; a token needs admin): destination, credential name (never its content), enabled, and the progress — pending_since, the last success, failures and the last FG code and reason. 404 FG-REPO-0005 when there is none.

commands.name: mirror set
commands.summary: Set a project's push mirror (an administrator, a person). The URL must be https, on mirror.allowed_hosts and without user information; --credential names a file of mirror.credentials_dir (one <username>:<token> line, mode 0600). 400 FG-INT-0021 otherwise. A new or re-enabled mirror is pushed at once.

commands.name: mirror remove
commands.summary: Remove a project's push mirror and its progress (an administrator, a person); GitLab keeps what it has. Needs --yes.

commands.name: mirror sync
commands.summary: Queue one push of every branch and tag to the mirror now (an administrator, a person); queued false means this request's push was already queued. 404 FG-REPO-0005 without an enabled mirror.
